findings.title: Destroying the request after sending 413 can surface an unhandled stream error
findings.evidence: On oversized bodies, the handler sends a 413 response and then immediately destroys the request stream without attaching any error handler that will run once settled is true.

findings.recommendation: After sending 413, stop reading without forcing an error, or destroy the request with an error only if you also consume or safely handle the resulting stream error after settlement. For example, remove listeners and return after ending the response, or keep the error handler active even when settled.

corroboration.reason: An 'error' listener is always attached to req before any data can arrive, so req.destroy() cannot produce an unhandled stream error — the listener existing is what prevents the throw, regardless of the early return when settled is true. Additionally, req.destroy() called without an error argument does not itself emit 'error'.
